summary: Sudden 5xx surge: apigw returning 502/503 and upstream runtime OOMs during Redis rate-limiter failover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MailFold) reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses and long tail streaming disconnects starting ~2026-03-13T18:12Z. API gateway returned a mix of 502/503 and short-lived 504s. Upstream serving runtimes for the customer's dedicated pool experienced worker restarts and OOM-like exits during the same window.

Impact:
- MailFold observed ~15-20% of requests failing with 5xx across chat and embedding routes for ~12 minutes.
- Streaming sessions dropped mid-stream; clients hit reconnect/retry loops.
- Customer-facing SLA alerts triggered; customer reported production user impact (message delivery failures).

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1), MailFold dedicated GPU pool (dedicated customer tenant).
- Rate-limiter backed by Redis (cluster B) and a local in-memory fallback.
- Autoscaler: dynamic HPA with prewarm policy.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Simulated Redis master failover occurred (external DB event at 18:10Z).
2) Rate-limiter client fell back to local token-bucket with conservative defaults.
3) Sudden retry/replay behavior from upstream client SDKs (hedged retries + prefetch churn) produced a high burst of simultaneous requests.
4) Serving-runtime prefetch workers attempted aggressive KV prefetch and hit kvcache lock contention; several runtime workers were OOM-killed by the watchdog.
5) API gateway started returning 502/503 as upstreams became unhealthy.

Observations / Logs / Metrics:
- apigw: 502/503 rate peaked at 18:14Z -> 19:00Z; customer 5xx% ~18.7% (per-route).
- runtime: repeated SIGABRT and watchdog restarts; kernel logs show out-of-memory events on several GPUs (nvml messages correlated).
- rate-limiter: Redis client reported connection timeouts and 'READONLY' during failover; fallback tokens depleted rapidly.
- kvcache: lock_wait_count increased 20x; eviction_rate spiked.

Relevant log excerpts (sanitized):
[2026-03-13T18:12:30Z] rate-limiter: redis timeout: IOERR: Connection reset by peer
[2026-03-13T18:13:02Z] serving-runtime[worker-14]: kvcache: lock_wait=132ms key=tenant-123/prefetch
[2026-03-13T18:13:47Z] runtime[worker-7]: OOM killer invoked: process_exit_status=137 nvml: memory allocation failed
[2026-03-13T18:14:02Z] apigw: upstream unhealthy for route /v1/chat/stream tenant=mailfold status=502

Current status:
- Incident declared and triaged by Support. SRE investigating runtime crashes and Redis failover correlation. Mitigation steps applied (see comments).
comments: 2026-03-13T18:16Z - Support (Liam O'Neill): Received initial alert from MailFold; gathered request IDs and sample call IDs. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE channel #sre-support.

2026-03-13T18:22Z - SRE (Riley Chen): Observed Redis failover at 18:10Z in cluster B; client SDK fell back to in-memory limiter which quickly drained. KVCACHE lock contention correlated with prefetch-heavy queries. Marking as likely backpressure + rate-limiter fallback amplification.

2026-03-13T18:30Z - Engineering (Priya Desai): Deployed temporary throttle on MailFold tenant at the API ingress to shed excess retries and disabled aggressive prefetch for that tenant. Noted immediate drop in 502s from 18:31Z. Preparing a more stable config roll-forward.

2026-03-13T19:05Z - Customer (MailFold support): Customer confirms request success rate improving after throttling; still seeing sporadic dropped streaming frames. Asked for timeline and permanent fix plan.
2026-03-13T20:10Z - SRE (Riley Chen): Applied longer-term mitigation: increased local token-bucket refill and added short circuit-breaker for prefetch queue depth. Monitoring for recurrence.
investigation_notes: Primary hypothesis: Redis master failover triggered a degraded rate-limiter fallback that did not backoff retries aggressively, producing a burst that amplified prefetch and KV lock contention in serving-runtime.
Supporting evidence: timestamps of Redis failover, rate-limiter timeouts, kvcache lock_wait spikes and runtime OOM logs all align within a 2-3 minute window before 5xx surge.

Contributing factors: MailFold's SDK hedged retry pattern (2 fast retries), combined chat + embedding mixed workload created high memory pressure on dedicated pool. Autoscaler prewarm thresholds didn't spin up capacity quickly enough under lock contention.
Related: suspected link to existing issues SUP-421999 (tls-session-cache corruption) and SUP-271999 (handoff thundering); these provide context on upstream health amplifiers.
Temporary mitigations validated: ingress shedding + disabling aggressive prefetch for tenant reduced 5xx rate to <1% within ~3 minutes of change.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied (temporary) on 2026-03-13: ingress-level request-shedding for MailFold and disabled tenant-specific aggressive prefetch. Increased in-memory token-bucket capacity and introduced a short-duration circuit-breaker for prefetch queue depth. Engineering to roll a safer fallback path when Redis is unavailable (ensure exponential backoff + jitter and avoid immediate replay).

Planned follow-ups:
- Patch rate-limiter client to use exponential backoff + jitter on Redis failover (PR referenced). Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce HPA cooldown for dedicated pools and add a reactive prewarm when kvcache lock_wait spikes. Owner: Platform SRE. ETA: 2026-03-22.
- Post-incident review and runbook update to include graceful Redis-failover behavior and tenant-specific prefetch caps. Postmortem scheduled on 2026-03-16.
- Customer-facing summary to be sent to MailFold by CS with timeline and follow-ups.
